directAnswer: To change default apps on a Mac, go to System Preferences, select 'General', and choose your preferred applications for web browsing, email, and more.
summary: Changing default apps on macOS allows you to customize which applications open specific file types and protocols.

sections.heading: Changing the Default Web Browser
sections.body: In the 'General' section of System Preferences, you can select your preferred web browser from the 'Default web browser' dropdown menu.

sections.heading: Changing the Default Email Client
sections.body: Similarly, in the 'General' preferences, choose your preferred email application from the 'Default email reader' dropdown.

sections.heading: Changing Default Applications for Specific File Types
sections.body: To change the default app for a specific file type, right-click the file, select 'Get Info', and under 'Open with', choose your desired app, then click 'Change All'.

steps.title: Open System Preferences
steps.detail: Click on the Apple menu in the top-left corner and select 'System Preferences'.

steps.title: Select General
steps.detail: In System Preferences, click on 'General' to access default app settings.

steps.title: Choose Default Apps
steps.detail: From the 'Default web browser' and 'Default email reader' dropdowns, select the applications you want to use.

steps.title: Set Default for File Types
steps.detail: Right-click a file, select 'Get Info', choose an app under 'Open with', and click 'Change All' to apply.

faqs.question: Can I set different default apps for different file types?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can set different default applications for various file types by using the 'Get Info' option on individual files.

faqs.question: Will changing the default app affect all users on the Mac?
faqs.answer: No, changing default apps only affects the current user account; other accounts will retain their own settings.

faqs.question: What if the app I want isn't listed?
faqs.answer: If the app isn't listed, you can select 'Other...' in the dropdown menus to browse and choose any installed application.

caveats: Some applications may not allow themselves to be set as default for certain file types.
